_note: Actor ids and defaults for research_gatherer/engine.py — the ONLY config it reads. No brand, avatar or room name lives here (workspace rule 7); those come from brands/<brand>/core-avatars/**/*.md at run time. No chain's stage map lives here either — that's each caller's own chain_profile.

caps._note: forums_per_run is the ~research var's own pull (cheap, cached 14 days); forums_per_deep is the deep-research trigger's default --cap, split across however many Schwartz questions fire; comments_per_post covers the swiped post's own thread; discovery is the ONE unrestricted search that finds which rooms an avatar actually talks in — small on purpose (~40 items ~ $__), cached like every other pull.

discovery._note: How the ONE room-finding search is fired. `relevance` is the door's own default and the right sort here, found the hard way on 2026-09-18: two live pulls with sort `top` came back with general-interest and film-trivia communities, because sorting an unrestricted search by score ranks the loudest posts on the platform that happen to share a word, not the posts about the topic. Relevance finds the topical rooms; the score weighting then picks the loudest of THOSE, which is what the weighting was always for. No room name lives here (workspace rule 7) - only how the search is shaped.

demographic_fit._note: THE MARKER TABLE — the owner ruled it 2026-09-18 after room discovery for a sun-damage sub-avatar returned three communities for a different set of people entirely: research has to be reconciled against the avatar's demographics or it is irrelevant for that avatar. Each row maps a marker found in a ROOM NAME to the demographic signal that room name carries. No brand, avatar or room of ours is named here (workspace rule 7) — these are generic community-naming conventions, the same ones any brand's discovery would hit, and the avatar's own demographics arrive at run time from brands/<brand>/core-avatars/**. A room whose name carries no marker is `general` and is always kept: the table can say a room is plainly for someone else, never that it is plainly for us.

age_bands._note: A marker's age value and an avatar's age slot are both read as a numeric band — `30+` is 30 and over, `13–24` is a closed band, and a slot is the widest range its own numbers describe. They clash only when the two bands do not overlap at all. A slot with no readable numbers is `unknown` and rules nothing out.

demographic_fit._match_rule: How a marker is looked for, in a room name and again in the avatar's own slot: the text is split into segments (on punctuation, on a camelCase boundary, and between letters and digits) and lowercased. A marker of 3 characters or fewer must EQUAL a whole segment, so `ph` finds `skincare_ph` and never `phimosis`; a longer marker must START a segment or a run of them, so `black` finds `blackskincare` and `men` never fires inside `women`. A room name carrying no marker is `general` and is always kept. The longer forms a PROFILE writes — `the United Kingdom`, `New Zealand` — are in the same lists, because the avatar's own slot is read with the same rule as the room name.

gates._note: How a gate behaves when it fails (research_gatherer/gates.py). elements: hold = an unknown doctrine technique or delivery dial named by a research question stops the pull before anything is spent; record = write it into check.json and pull anyway (the behaviour before 2026-09-20). inputs and delivery have no mode: they record what the engine already refused.

ownvoice._note: gather.py ownvoice — our own audience (ad comments + support emails) into the avatar's bank. Brand sources come from brands/<brand>/operations/brand.json, never from here. model = the Claude model the sort prompt (prompts/ownvoice-sort.md) runs on; posts_per_run = how many top-spend ad posts are scraped for comments; first_run_since = where a brand's first run starts when it has no state yet.
